statement:
For any integer $n\ge0$,
$$\int_n^{n+1} f(x)\,dx = n+1.$$

Evaluate
$$\int_0^3 f(x)\,dx + \int_1^3 f(x)\,dx + \int_2^3 f(x)\,dx + \int_4^3 f(x)\,dx + \int_5^3 f(x)\,dx.$$
solution:
Split each integral into unit intervals using $\int_a^b=\int_a^c+\int_c^b$:

$$\int_0^3 f = \int_0^1 f + \int_1^2 f + \int_2^3 f = 1+2+3 = 6,$$
$$\int_1^3 f = \int_1^2 f + \int_2^3 f = 2+3 = 5,$$
$$\int_2^3 f = 3.$$

For the last two, reverse the limits using $\int_a^b f = -\int_b^a f$:
$$\int_4^3 f = -\int_3^4 f = -4,$$
$$\int_5^3 f = -\int_3^5 f = -\left(\int_3^4 f + \int_4^5 f\right) = -(4+5) = -9.$$

Adding all five:
$$6+5+3-4-9 = 1,$$
which is **option C**.
hints: Use additivity to split integrals like ∫0^3 into unit intervals.
For ∫4^3 and ∫5^3, reverse the limits (they are negative).
